StackType.issue: Closed 2026-07-30 (tier-2 campaign): (Task 25.) The 15 `on_stack` no-op overrides are DELETED; the base `Power.on_stack` adds, matching PowerCmd.ModifyAmount (PowerCmd.cs:236), which adds unconditionally with no StackType branch -- PowerStackType.Single means 'Amount is hidden and displayed as 1' (PowerStackType.cs:10-13), not 'does not stack'. All 16 units re-verified against their own C#: 15 are StackType.Single, and NONE overrides InstanceType (PowerModel.cs:144 default None), so none needs T1's instance machinery instead of amount-adding. Two per-site exceptions, both verified: (1) DAMPEN's C# StackType is actually `None`, not Single (DampenPower.cs:22) -- the queue's 16-unit list was wrong about it; its only applier, MagiKnight, dedupes caller-side (MagiKnight.cs:78-96: re-application calls AddCaster only and never reaches PowerCmd.Apply), so the deletion is inert through the real caller and T28's caster-set machinery is untouched and re-pinned. (2) HEX genuinely reads Amount (HexPower.cs:79 feeds CardCmd.Afflict<Hexed>(card, Amount)), so this deletion closes a real divergence that remains DORMANT only because SpectralKnight's move machine never loops back to HEX and KnightsElite fields exactly one -- a second Hex applier makes it live. ILLUSION needed no override and is unchanged (the opposite-sign case the record notes). No reachable re-application among the other 13: Burrowed and Soar re-apply only after their own expire/remove, always onto a fresh instance. Pins: test/test_stack_type_single.py (39 tests).  The text it replaced read: PowerStackType.Single, and the sim overrides on_stack to `pass` citing it. Per the settled census (`py audit/tools/power_census.py stack`) that reasoning is wrong: Single means "Amount is hidden and is always 1" (PowerStackType.cs:10-13) and PowerCmd.ModifyAmount (PowerCmd.cs:236) adds unconditionally with no StackType branch. DORMANT here for a reason specific to this power and worth stating: Soar's multiplier reads `DynamicVars["DamageDecrease"]`, NOT Amount (SoarPower.cs:29), so no C# behaviour depends on the amount either. The only ported applier applies it once and removes it on the dive (monsters/glory/owl_magistrate.py:59-60; OwlMagistrate.cs:134 apply, :146 PowerCmd.Remove<SoarPower>). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

ModifyDamageMultiplicative.rationale: Constant checked: C# returns `DynamicVars["DamageDecrease"].BaseValue / 100m` and CanonicalVars declares `new DynamicVar("DamageDecrease", 50m)` (SoarPower.cs:17), i.e. exactly 0.5, which is what powers.py:3071 hard-codes. 0.5 is dyadic, so it is outside hook_dispatch G9's float-product problem (`py audit/tools/power_census.py multipliers` lists it as dyadic). `target != base.Owner -> 1m` matches powers.py:3070. The `!props.IsPoweredAttack() -> 1m` guard is carried separately below.

guards.rationale: The sim omits the per-power test and relies on the PIPELINE-level gate instead: cmds.py:56-58 runs modify_damage_additive/modify_damage_multiplicative only when `is_powered_attack(props)` (valueprops.py:47-49, Move && !Unpowered). C# never gates the dispatcher -- CreatureCmd.cs:261 calls Hook.ModifyDamage with ModifyDamageHookType.All for every damage type and Hook.ModifyDamageInternal (Hook.cs:2515-2538) calls every listener -- so the gate lives in each override. Equivalent HERE because this power's C# override does self-gate. The hoisting itself is damage_pipeline gap G3 and is not re-verdicted per rule 3. Independently reproduced: `py audit/tools/power_slot_probes.py ungated-modifiers` finds 37 gated vs 9 ungated C# Modify{Damage,Block}{Additive,Multiplicative} overrides. Third-file citations, not hashed here.
